Dionysiaca.fact: The Dionysiaca (Ancient Greek: Διονυσιακά, Dionysiaká) is an Ancient Greek epic poem by the 5th-century AD poet Nonnus.

Dionysiaca.fact: Totaling 48 books and 21,286 lines, it is the longest surviving poem from Greco-Roman antiquity.

Dionysiaca.question: It is especially remarkable that _____ was so exacting with meter because the quantitative meter of classical poetry was giving way in Nonnus' time to stressed meter
Dionysiaca.fact: While Homer has 32 varieties of hexameter lines, Nonnus only employs 9 variations, avoids elision, employs mostly weak caesurae, and follows a variety of euphonic and syllabic rules regarding word placement. It is especially remarkable that Nonnus was so exacting with meter because the quantitative meter of classical poetry was giving way in Nonnus' time to stressed meter.

Dionysiaca.fact: While Homer has 32 varieties of hexameter lines, Nonnus only employs 9 variations, avoids elision, employs mostly weak caesurae, and follows a variety of euphonic and syllabic rules regarding word placement. Dionysiaca.fact: The appearance of Proteus, a shapeshifting god, in the proem (preamble) serves as a metaphor for Nonnus' varied style.

Dionysiaca.subject: Indian Languages
Dionysiaca.question: As with many other late classical poets, newer scholarship has avoided the value-laden judgments of 19th-century scholars and attempted to reassess and rehabilitate _____' works

Nonnus' compendious accounts of Dionysiac legend and his use of variant traditions and lost sources have encouraged scholars to use him as a channel to recover lost Hellenistic poetry and mythic traditions.
